maria: Heads-up — several customers reporting 502/504s from the hosted inference API since ~09:12 UTC. Gateway logs show cache dependency errors (Redis auth failures) and fallthrough to memcached which is timing out.

kevin: Any example request IDs or customer accounts we can point to for repro?

maria: customer A: req_id=rx-9a3f, customer B: req_id=rz-4b2c. Attaching a minimal trace/log snippet below.

maria: ```
[2026-03-17T09:14:02Z] gateway INFO route=/v1/generate status=502 err="cache: redis auth failed: ERR invalid password" trace_id=rx-9a3f
[2026-03-17T09:14:03Z] runtime WARN model=redwood-slim kv_hit=false fallback=memcached err="conn_timeout" trace_id=rx-9a3f
```

li: Looking at prometheus: prefix_cache_auth_failures spiked at 09:11->09:15 (x120), redis_connection_errors same window. Memcached error rate increased but later than redis auth failures. Graphs: https://grafana.company/graph?panelId=42&from=09:00&to=09:30

jordan: Did we rotate any KMS/redis passwords around 09:10? Ops runbook shows a key mapping change for prefix cache earlier this morning. @ops-bot any deploy events?

ops-bot: deploy: config-rollout/4567 completed at 2026-03-17T09:10:18Z by infra:ops. Changes: prefix-cache KMS mapping -> new-key-id.

kevin: That aligns. Likely misapplied/new-key not reachable -> redis auth error -> cache fallthrough -> memcached overloaded -> gateway 502s.

maria: Customers are seeing degraded UX; raised a support incident and informed SRE/Runtime. Ticket ENG-10123 created.

billing-bot: Not seeing a billing quota or billing spikes tied to those customers yet — it's primarily increased retries causing more runtime calls.

kevin: Short-term mitigation suggestions: 1) revert KMS mapping or re-apply correct redis creds; 2) enable cache circuit breaker (fail open) to avoid memcached fanout; 3) scale up memcached shard pool if needed.

jordan: I can flip the circuit breaker and temporarily route requests to the warm model pool to reduce origin pain. Command to disable prefix cache for hosted API: ```
rwctl config set service.cache.prefix.enabled false --scope=hosted --reason="mitigation: redis auth failures"
```

ops-bot: Command executed by jordan at 2026-03-17T09:18:05Z: success.

li: Metrics after circuit flip: prefix cache auth errors drop to 0 (auth path short-circuited), memcached errors fall ~80%, gateway 5xx rate down to baseline by 09:22. Origin latency increased ~30ms (expected).

maria: Notifying impacted customers with the mitigation note and ETA for fix.

kevin: Next steps for runtime: revert the KMS mapping or patch KMS->redis creds, add a health-check gating for credential rollout, and add an automated rollback if cache auth failures exceed threshold during rollout.

jordan: I'll own the rollback/patch and postmortem. Assigning ENG-10123 to eng-runtime.

maria: I'll follow up with a support status update and bundle customer repro info (req ids + timestamps).

li: Recommend postmortem items: (a) test KMS mapping in staging with live auth, (b) add a pre-apply canary that hits a small percentage of traffic, (c) add alert runbook for prefix cache auth spikes that auto-fires circuit breaker.

maria: Thanks all. Will post the support thread update once customers are notified. :white_check_mark:

kevin: Good catch. Marking incident mitigated for now. Please keep this thread updated if any regressions. :thumbsup:
